intro.text: A number sign (#) is used with this entry because of evidence that retinitis pigmentosa-7 (RP7) is caused by heterozygous mutation in the peripherin-2 gene (PRPH2; 179605) on chromosome 6p21.1. Digenic retinitis pigmentosa is caused by double heterozygosity for mutations in PRPH2 and in the unlinked ROM1 gene (180721).

checks.claim: Retinitis pigmentosa-7 (RP7) is caused by heterozygous mutation in the peripherin-2 gene (PRPH2).
checks.evidence_quote: We report here three mutations of the human homologue of the rds gene (RDS) that cosegregate with autosomal dominant retinitis pigmentosa in separate families. Our results indicate that some cases of autosomal dominant retinitis pigmentosa are due to mutations at the RDS locus.
checks.explanation: The abstract links RDS (PRPH2) mutations to autosomal dominant RP, which implies heterozygosity. It does not use the RP7 designation, does not say outright that the mutations are heterozygous, and says only 'some cases' of adRP. Only the abstract was supplied.

checks.claim: The PRPH2 gene is located on chromosome 6p21.1.
checks.evidence_quote: A third adRP gene in a large Irish pedigree has been mapped to chromosome 6p, showing tight linkage with the gene for peripherin
checks.explanation: The abstract puts the peripherin gene on chromosome 6p. The finer band 6p21.1 is standard location nomenclature that only restates this placement in more detail, which the instructions count as supported.

checks.claim: Digenic retinitis pigmentosa is caused by double heterozygosity for mutations in PRPH2 and in the ROM1 gene.
checks.evidence_quote: Three families were identified with mutations in the unlinked photoreceptor-specific genes ROM1 and peripherin/RDS, in which only double heterozygotes develop retinitis pigmentosa (RP).
checks.explanation: The abstract says that only double heterozygates for ROM1 and peripherin/RDS (PRPH2) mutations develop RP, which it calls digenic RP.

checks.claim: The ROM1 gene is unlinked to the PRPH2 gene.
checks.evidence_quote: Digenic retinitis pigmentosa due to mutations at the unlinked peripherin/RDS and ROM1 loci.
checks.explanation: The paper explicitly calls the ROM1 and peripherin/RDS loci unlinked.

paragraphs.text: Retinitis pigmentosa-7 is a form of autosomal dominant retinitis pigmentosa (adRP). Jordan et al. (1992), who referred to the disorder as RP6, linked it to the gene encoding peripherin-RDS, a photoreceptor-specific protein. Retinitis pigmentosa is characterized by photoreceptor degeneration (Kajiwara et al., 1991). Wang et al. (2013) noted that patients with juvenile RP later develop night blindness and narrowed visual fields, and eventually severe vision impairment. A digenic form of RP has also been reported (Wang et al., 2013), in which affected individuals are double heterozygotes for mutations in peripherin/RDS and ROM1 (Kajiwara et al., 1994).

checks.claim: Retinitis pigmentosa-7 is a form of autosomal dominant retinitis pigmentosa (adRP).
checks.evidence_quote: late-onset autosomal dominant retinitis pigmentosa (adRP; RP6)
checks.explanation: The paper describes the disorder as adRP but calls it RP6. The 'retinitis pigmentosa-7' name does not appear in the abstract.

checks.claim: Jordan et al. (1992) referred to the disorder now designated retinitis pigmentosa-7 as RP6.
checks.evidence_quote: Autosomal dominant retinitis pigmentosa (adRP; RP6): cosegregation of RP6 and the peripherin-RDS locus
checks.explanation: The paper uses the name RP6. The current RP7 name is OMIM nomenclature.

checks.claim: Jordan et al. (1992) linked the autosomal dominant retinitis pigmentosa to the gene encoding peripherin-RDS.
checks.evidence_quote: Incorporation of these data into a multipoint analysis produced a lod score for adRP of 8.21, maximizing at the peripherin-RDS locus.
checks.explanation: The linkage peaked at the peripherin-RDS locus, and the authors suggest the gene has a role in this form of adRP.

checks.claim: Peripherin-RDS is a photoreceptor-specific protein.
checks.evidence_quote: the gene encoding peripherin-RDS, a photoreceptor-specific protein
checks.explanation: The abstract states this directly.

checks.claim: Retinitis pigmentosa is characterized by photoreceptor degeneration.
checks.evidence_quote: retinitis pigmentosa, one of the scores of hereditary human retinal degenerations, which is also characterized by photoreceptor degeneration
checks.explanation: The abstract says this directly.

checks.claim: Wang et al. (2013) noted that patients with juvenile retinitis pigmentosa later develop night blindness.
checks.evidence_quote: Juvenile RP patients appear to have better visual function at birth than those with LCA, and later develop night blindness, narrowed visual fields, and eventually severe vision impairment.
checks.explanation: The paper states this directly.

checks.claim: Wang et al. (2013) noted that patients with juvenile retinitis pigmentosa later develop narrowed visual fields.
checks.evidence_quote: Juvenile RP patients appear to have better visual function at birth than those with LCA, and later develop night blindness, narrowed visual fields, and eventually severe vision impairment.
checks.explanation: The paper states this directly.

checks.claim: Wang et al. (2013) noted that patients with juvenile retinitis pigmentosa eventually develop severe vision impairment.
checks.evidence_quote: Juvenile RP patients appear to have better visual function at birth than those with LCA, and later develop night blindness, narrowed visual fields, and eventually severe vision impairment.
checks.explanation: The paper states this directly.

checks.claim: A digenic form of retinitis pigmentosa has been reported.
checks.evidence_quote: the p.L185P mutation, together with a null mutation in ROM1, has been reported to cause digenic RP
checks.explanation: The paper mentions that digenic RP has been reported.

checks.claim: In digenic retinitis pigmentosa, affected individuals are double heterozygotes for mutations in peripherin/RDS and ROM1.
checks.evidence_quote: Three families were identified with mutations in the unlinked photoreceptor-specific genes ROM1 and peripherin/RDS, in which only double heterozygotes develop retinitis pigmentosa (RP).
checks.explanation: The abstract states this directly.

paragraphs.text: Kajiwara et al. (1994) established digenic inheritance of retinitis pigmentosa in families who were double heterozygous for mutations in PRPH2 and ROM1.

checks.claim: Kajiwara et al. (1994) established digenic inheritance of retinitis pigmentosa.
checks.evidence_quote: These findings indicate that the allelic and nonallelic heterogeneity known to be a feature of monogenic RP is complicated further by interactions between unlinked mutations causing digenic RP.
checks.explanation: The paper reports digenic RP. The abstract says 'indicate' rather than 'established', but the claim is a fair summary.

checks.claim: In the families studied by Kajiwara et al. (1994), individuals with retinitis pigmentosa were double heterozygous for mutations in PRPH2 and ROM1.
checks.evidence_quote: Three families were identified with mutations in the unlinked photoreceptor-specific genes ROM1 and peripherin/RDS, in which only double heterozygotes develop retinitis pigmentosa (RP).
checks.explanation: The abstract states this directly.

paragraphs.text: Jordan et al. (1992) found that an intragenic marker derived from the peripherin-RDS gene cosegregated with the adRP disease locus with zero recombination (lod score 5.46 at theta = 0.00).

checks.claim: Jordan et al. (1992) found that an intragenic marker derived from the peripherin-RDS gene cosegregated with the autosomal dominant retinitis pigmentosa disease locus with zero recombination.
checks.evidence_quote: an intrageneic marker derived from this gene cosegregated with the adRP disease locus with zero recombination
checks.explanation: The abstract states this directly.

checks.claim: Jordan et al. (1992) obtained a lod score of 5.46 at theta = 0.00 for linkage between the peripherin-RDS intragenic marker and the autosomal dominant retinitis pigmentosa locus.
checks.evidence_quote: cosegregated with the adRP disease locus with zero recombination (lod score 5.46 at q = .00)
checks.explanation: The abstract writes 'q' where the draft writes theta; both mean the same recombination fraction.

paragraphs.text: In a large Irish pedigree with adRP mapped to chromosome 6p and showing tight linkage with the peripherin gene, Farrar et al. (1991) identified a 3-bp deletion in that gene.

checks.claim: Farrar et al. (1991) studied a large Irish pedigree with autosomal dominant retinitis pigmentosa.
checks.evidence_quote: A third adRP gene in a large Irish pedigree has been mapped to chromosome 6p
checks.explanation: The abstract describes a large Irish pedigree with autosomal dominant RP (adRP).

checks.claim: The autosomal dominant retinitis pigmentosa in the large Irish pedigree studied by Farrar et al. (1991) mapped to chromosome 6p.
checks.evidence_quote: A third adRP gene in a large Irish pedigree has been mapped to chromosome 6p
checks.explanation: The abstract states that the disease gene in this pedigree mapped to 6p.

checks.claim: The autosomal dominant retinitis pigmentosa in the large Irish pedigree studied by Farrar et al. (1991) showed tight linkage with the peripherin gene.
checks.evidence_quote: showing tight linkage with the gene for peripherin, a photoreceptor cell-specific glycoprotein
checks.explanation: The abstract states tight linkage with the peripherin gene.

checks.claim: Farrar et al. (1991) identified a 3-bp deletion in the peripherin gene in the large Irish pedigree with autosomal dominant retinitis pigmentosa.
checks.evidence_quote: We have now identified a three-base-pair deletion which results in the loss of one of a pair of highly conserved cysteine residues in the predicted third transmembrane domain of peripherin. This deletion segregates with the disease phenotype
checks.explanation: The abstract reports a 3-bp deletion in peripherin that segregates with the disease in this pedigree.

paragraphs.text: Kajiwara et al. (1991) reported 3 mutations in RDS, the human homolog of the mouse retinal degeneration slow (rds) gene, that cosegregated with autosomal dominant retinitis pigmentosa in separate families.

checks.claim: RDS is the human homolog of the mouse retinal degeneration slow (rds) gene.
checks.evidence_quote: the human homologue of the rds gene (RDS)
checks.explanation: The abstract says RDS is the human homolog of the murine rds gene.

checks.claim: Kajiwara et al. (1991) reported 3 mutations in the RDS gene.
checks.evidence_quote: We report here three mutations of the human homologue of the rds gene (RDS)
checks.explanation: The abstract reports three mutations.

checks.claim: The 3 RDS mutations reported by Kajiwara et al. (1991) cosegregated with autosomal dominant retinitis pigmentosa in separate families.
checks.evidence_quote: three mutations of the human homologue of the rds gene (RDS) that cosegregate with autosomal dominant retinitis pigmentosa in separate families
checks.explanation: The abstract says this directly.

paragraphs.text: Kajiwara et al. (1994) described digenic retinitis pigmentosa in 3 families with mutations in the unlinked photoreceptor-specific genes ROM1 and peripherin/RDS. Only double heterozygotes developed RP, implying that family members carrying only one of the mutations were unaffected.

checks.claim: Kajiwara et al. (1994) described digenic retinitis pigmentosa in 3 families.
checks.evidence_quote: Three families were identified with mutations in the unlinked photoreceptor-specific genes ROM1 and peripherin/RDS
checks.explanation: The abstract gives the same number of families: three.

checks.claim: The 3 families with digenic retinitis pigmentosa described by Kajiwara et al. (1994) had mutations in ROM1 and peripherin/RDS.
checks.evidence_quote: Three families were identified with mutations in the unlinked photoreceptor-specific genes ROM1 and peripherin/RDS
checks.explanation: The abstract states this directly.

checks.claim: ROM1 and peripherin/RDS are unlinked photoreceptor-specific genes.
checks.evidence_quote: the unlinked photoreceptor-specific genes ROM1 and peripherin/RDS
checks.explanation: The abstract states this directly.

checks.claim: In the families studied by Kajiwara et al. (1994), only double heterozygotes for ROM1 and peripherin/RDS mutations developed retinitis pigmentosa.
checks.evidence_quote: in which only double heterozygotes develop retinitis pigmentosa (RP)
checks.explanation: The abstract states this directly.

checks.claim: In the families studied by Kajiwara et al. (1994), family members carrying only one of the ROM1 or peripherin/RDS mutations were unaffected.
checks.evidence_quote: in which only double heterozygotes develop retinitis pigmentosa (RP)
checks.explanation: If only double heterozygotes develop RP, family members with just one of the mutations are unaffected. This follows directly from the abstract.

paragraphs.text: Wang et al. (2013) noted that work from Molday and coworkers had established that the L185P peripherin mutant is conditionally defective with respect to subunit assembly, being capable of forming peripherin dimers but not tetramers.

checks.claim: Wang et al. (2013) noted that the L185P peripherin mutant is conditionally defective with respect to subunit assembly.
checks.evidence_quote: Work from Molday and co-workers established that this peripherin mutant is conditionally defective with respect to subunit assembly, and is capable of forming peripherin dimers but not tetramers.
checks.explanation: In context, 'this peripherin mutant' refers to p.L185P.

checks.claim: Wang et al. (2013) noted that the L185P peripherin mutant can form peripherin dimers but not tetramers.
checks.evidence_quote: Work from Molday and co-workers established that this peripherin mutant is conditionally defective with respect to subunit assembly, and is capable of forming peripherin dimers but not tetramers.
checks.explanation: The paper states this directly, referring to p.L185P.
